subject: Post-call: model fit & benchmarks for Acme Health
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.ai>
To: Sophia Chen <sophia.chen@acmehealth.com>, Bob Jenkins <bob.jenkins@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 06 Sep 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: model fit & benchmarks for Acme Health

Hi Sophia / Bob —

Thanks again for a great call this morning. Quick recap + proposed next steps based on what we heard:

Recap:
- Primary goals: faster triage of clinical notes (classification + extractive QA) and high precision on sensitive fields.
- Target throughput: ~100–250 requests/sec during peak business hours.
- Latency SLO: target P95 < 250ms for the user-facing flows.
- Data constraints: PHI in transit; you need VPC/private deployment for production.

Preliminary model fit / recommendations:
- Latency-sensitive (recommended for early prod): llama-2-13b (q4_0) on Dedicated nodes — good latency/price balance.
- Quality-first (for highest F1 on extraction): llama-2-70b (8-bit quant) on Dedicated; higher throughput cost but better accuracy on long clinical contexts.
- For embeddings/semantic search: sentence-transformer-redwood-3.1 (FP16).

Redwood-verified perf snapshot (summary from our run with your sample prompt set):
- Throughput (TPS): 160 req/s (batch size 8) on a 4xA100 pool
- Latency: P50 = 78ms, P95 = 220ms, P99 = 370ms
- Notes: P99 increases significantly for >4k token contexts due to KV cache pressure — see linked profile.

Artifacts I attached/linked:
- redwood_benchmark_acmehealth_20260905.pdf (benchmark summary, run configs)
- acme_prompt_set_v1.json (your sample prompts we ran)
- Perf profile: https://console.redwood.ai/models/verified/perf/acmehealth-profile-20260905
- Full benchmark: https://drive.redwood.ai/benchmarks/acmehealth-20260905

Next steps I propose:
1) Confirm which model/config you want for a 1-week eval: latency-first or quality-first.
2) If OK, we spin up a dedicated eval job using your prompt set (no cost for the first eval).
3) Schedule a 30-min follow-up next Tue/Wed to review results and cost estimates.

Quick ask: can you confirm whether your procurement team needs a security package (SOC2 + VPC) added before we run the private eval?

Thanks —
Alex Martinez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
alex@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

Thanks Alex — helpful summary. A couple quick questions after scanning the benchmark PDF:

- Can you confirm P99 latency at 95th percentile load (i.e., sustained 200 TPS)? The P99 of 370ms you shared — is that at burst or sustained?
- What's the estimated cost to serve ~1M generated tokens / month for the latency-first config?
- For the quality-first (70b) option — any guidance on fallback strategies if we hit a capacity event (auto-fallback to 13b?)

Also, procurement asked whether the private eval will require us to sign off on a PO before the trial. We prefer to avoid PO paperwork for the eval if possible.

—Sophia

Dir. Product, Acme Health

Hi Sophia — good questions. Quick answers below:

- P99 at sustained 200 TPS: in our dedicated config runs we measured ~420ms P99 when you sustain 200 TPS for >5 minutes due to cache-warmup and KV pressure. We can mitigate with slightly larger pool (burst nodes) or prefix/KV caching tuned to your prompt patterns.
- Cost estimate (very rough): latency-first (13b q4) ~ $1,200–1,800 / month for 1M generated tokens on Dedicated with autoscaling capped. Quality-first (70b 8-bit) ~ $6,500–9,000 / month for the same token volume. I can run precise calc with your token-length distribution.
- Fallbacks: we recommend an automatic routing policy — prefer 70b when capacity available, fallback to 13b (same prompt set) when under pressure. Redwood supports canary rollouts + automatic fallback to a compatible variant to preserve availability.

Procurement: we can run a 1-week private eval without a PO under a short trial agreement (we'll provide a trial addendum). I'll loop in our legal ops if you want that in writing — typically not required for a short non-prod eval.

If you give the go-ahead I can schedule the eval and provision the cluster this week. Proposed times for 30-min review: Tue 9/8 10:00am PT or Wed 9/9 2:00pm PT — which works?

Thanks,
Alex

If you want, Dylan and I can stand up the eval and share the raw results dashboard ahead of the sync.
